people.label: John Callahan
people.sub: Federal Aviation Administration manager at Washington headquarters in the mid-1980s; the FAA official who in 2000 and 2001 publicly described the agency's handling of the Japan Air Lines 1628 case of 17 November 1986
people.narrative: John Callahan is the most useful witness the Disclosure Project produced and the reason is not him. The event he describes is one of the very few claims in this cluster with a large federal record that owes nothing whatever to Steven Greer: over 1,500 pages at the National Archives in Record Group 237, archival identifier 733667, containing the air traffic control transcript, the FAA's own forms, dated January 1987 interviews with all three Japan Air Lines crew members, Captain Terauchi's written statement in Japanese and in translation, and the FAA Alaskan Region's press release of 5 March 1987. That record exists whether or not Callahan ever spoke, and it was recovered only because John Greenewald kept asking for seventeen years after the FAA wrote to him on 27 June 2001 that the documents would be destroyed in thirty days. The asymmetry is the whole point of this node. The case is documented to an unusual depth; the man's claimed office is not. He says, in the Briefing Document and at the National Press Club, that he was Division Chief of the Accidents and Investigations Branch at FAA headquarters for about six years. The researcher who set out in 2015 specifically to confirm that found, in his own words, that only four references to a John Callahan at the FAA came up and that none of them matched the claimed area; what the public record showed was a Quality Control Branch Manager on the Quality Assurance Staff under the Associate Administrator for Air Traffic. The document eventually published in support of the claimed title is an OMB Form 171, a Personal Qualifications Statement, which Callahan handed the researcher himself in 2015. Its dates are consistent with the incident falling inside his tenure and they reconcile the researcher's negative finding with Callahan's account, so it is a point in his favour, but a form supplied by its own subject is not an agency release and this board does not score it as one. Nothing about that weakens the FAA file. It is why the case node beside this one matters more than the person node.
people.tierRationale: Node tier B: proximity, not credibility. He sits adjacent to a real agency record rather than inside any programme, and the record is the reason for the tier. Custody proximity 0 because no opened record places him in contact with any material. Access 0 because the only document for his access is one he supplied himself, and this board does not score A on a document that has never left the subject's hands; his claimed title is contradicted by the first pass anyone made through the public record. Disclosure role 3 because his entire public function since 2000 has been the publication of this case, and he carried into public view an agency file that the agency had twice said was destroyed. Status 'unknown' and no date: no obituary or death record for this John Callahan was opened.

people.label: Clifford E. Stone
people.sub: US Army sergeant, 1968 to 1990, whose documented assignments were clerical and administrative; claimant from the 1990s of service on Army crash-retrieval teams recovering craft and occupants
people.narrative: Clifford Stone is on this board because the evidence against his extraordinary account is unusually good, not because the account is. His ordinary career is a federal record and it was obtained: Philip J. Klass requested it from the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis and printed the assignments in the summer of 2001, and they run clerk/typist from basic training, clerk/typist in Vietnam from February 1970 to August 1972, administration specialist from March 1975, seven years in Germany, detachment sergeant, and from May 1985 chief administrative clerk at the New Mexico Military Institute. Kevin Randle, who is already a node on this board, who met Stone in February 1989 and visited his home many times, independently records the same shape: four claimed Vietnam tours against a record showing thirty-seven months overseas and not all of it in Vietnam, and nothing in the record supporting the story of slipping out at night to hunt the enemy. Those are two genuinely independent methods, a records request and a thirty-year acquaintance, and one of the two men spent his career arguing that other UFO cases are real. But the item that matters most is not an absence at all. It is something Stone did. He told the Disclosure Project that an Army team took him to Bentwaters in England in late December 1980 to investigate the incident there. On 23 December 1983, three years later, he filed a Freedom of Information Act request with the United States Air Force asking for information about that same incident, from his home address, without indicating that he was a serving Army sergeant. A man who had been there officially does not write in as a member of the public for the file. The record also contains something in his favour and it belongs here: after he was relieved for administrative inefficiency in January 1988, an Army investigation cleared him and he was later awarded the Meritorious Service Medal for the work he had been criticised over.

Custody proximity 0 because his claimed handling of recovered material is a claim and this board does not score C on a claim. Access 0 because no clearance, unit assignment or billet supporting the claimed access appears anywhere in the service record that was obtained, and a claimed clearance scores zero. Disclosure role 3 because his documented public function from the 1990s was the publication of the claim and a long campaign of FOIA requests. Date of death 10 February 2021 at Roswell, New Mexico, per Randle.

people.label: Robert M. Jacobs
people.sub: USAF lieutenant, Officer-in-Charge of Photo-optical Instrumentation, 1369th Photographic Squadron, Vandenberg AFB, 1963 to 1966; later an academic; claimant from 1982 about the Big Sur missile-test filming of September 1964
people.narrative: Robert Jacobs is the one witness in this cluster whose claimed role is confirmed by an independent named participant, and the confirmation comes from the man who spent a published article demolishing his interpretation. He published his own account twelve years before the Disclosure Project existed, in the MUFON UFO Journal of January 1989, giving his post as Officer-in-Charge of Photo-optical Instrumentation in the 1369th Photographic Squadron at Vandenberg Air Force Base from May 1963 to May 1966. In 1993 Kingston A. George, who identifies himself in his opening line as the project engineer for the experiment, answered him in the Skeptical Inquirer, and in the course of doing so confirmed that Jacobs was named on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron and managed the logistics at the Big Sur location, published photographs of the team and captioned Jacobs into and out of them, named the launch and gave its date, and cited a contemporaneous internal Air Force staff study by title and date. That is the rarest evidentiary shape on this board: two first-person published accounts by two people who were both there, agreeing about who was present and disagreeing about what the film showed. George's counter-explanation is that the imagery was decoy and chaff deployment, that the alarm which followed was about a classified weapons vulnerability rather than anything extraterrestrial, and that Jacobs was not cleared to interpret what he had seen. Jacobs's own dating is uncertain in his own article, which gives 2, 3 or 15 September 1964, while George fixes the event at dawn on 22 September 1964. The board should build this node on the 1989 publication and not on the Briefing Document, which arrived last and adds nothing but a date.
people.tierRationale: Node tier B: his post and his presence at a real Air Force test deployment are documented by two independent published participants, which puts him closer to a documented activity than any other witness in this pass. Custody proximity 0: the object of the claim is photographic film, not material or craft, and the film is stated by the project engineer to have been destroyed. Access 1 rather than 0 because the post itself is documented, and rather than 2 because the specific access at issue is documented as NOT held: the project engineer states in print that Jacobs 'was technically not authorized to view the pictures we were collecting' and that 'I don't think Bob Jacobs ever gained the required clearance.' Disclosure role 3 because he published the claim himself in 1982 and 1989 and has restated it since.

people.label: Larry Warren
people.sub: USAF security specialist who says he was assigned to the 81st Tactical Fighter Wing at RAF Bentwaters in December 1980; co-author of Left at East Gate, a book his co-author repudiated and his publisher withdrew
people.narrative: Larry Warren is carried here for the dispute rather than for the claim, because the dispute is documented and the claim is not. What is not in dispute is his assignment: his own co-author, after repudiating almost everything else, still accepts as authentic the handwritten letter Warren sent his mother in January 1981 and says explicitly that its authenticity does not carry the rest. What is in dispute is his presence at the events and the documentary evidence he produced for it. The case against him was not assembled by sceptics. Peter Robbins wrote Left at East Gate with him and defended it for twenty-nine years before publishing a statement on 13 June 2017 alleging, among other things, that a USAF Form 490 in the book's evidence carries an ophthalmic notation attributed to a physician Robbins found to be an orthopaedic surgeon, that a photograph purporting to show Warren with John Lennon is fabricated, that signatures on an in-processing sheet do not match, and that testimonial letters attributed to two named fellow airmen were never sent. Four months later the publisher, Cosimo, Inc., announced it was suspending distribution of the book because some of the experiences described in it 'may be inaccurate or embellished'. The senior officer on the record, Col. Charles Halt, is reported as saying Warren was not there; that strand reaches this board only through summaries and is graded Tier 3 until something Halt wrote is opened. The Briefing Document's own editorial header asserts that Warren is corroborated by Nick Pope, Lord Hill-Norton and Clifford Stone, but two of those three are witnesses inside the same document and one of them is Stone, whose service record is on this board.

entities.label: Japan Air Lines flight 1628, Alaska, 17 November 1986
entities.sub: A civil-aviation incident with a 1,500-page federal file at the National Archives, an FAA investigation, an agency press release concluding against a second aircraft, and a documented seventeen-year FOIA recovery
entities.desc: THIS IS THE NODE IN THIS CLUSTER WITH A REAL AGENCY RECORD, AND IT SHOULD CARRY MORE WEIGHT THAN THE WITNESS BESIDE IT. On the evening of 17 November 1986 a Japan Air Lines 747 crossing Alaskan airspace reported an object accompanying it; the FAA investigated, and the paper it generated survives in volume. The Black Vault asked for it in May 2001 and was told in a letter of 27 June 2001 that everything would be destroyed within thirty days; asked again in 2009 and was told it had been destroyed; and then found over 1,500 pages of it at the National Archives in Record Group 237, local identifier 1203, archival identifier 733667. The archive itemises 1,569 pages across thirty-five or more documents: FAA Form 8020-5 Aircraft Incident Record, FAA Form 3112, FAA Form 1600-32-1 interview notes, Captain Terauchi's written statement in Japanese and in English translation, dated transcripts of interviews with all three crew members in January 1987, radar data and computer plots, and a folder of correspondence with Philip Klass and Richard Haines. The agency's conclusion is equally on the record and it is negative: the FAA Alaskan Region's press release of 5 March 1987 states that its experts determined the second radar target was not another aircraft but an uncorrelated primary and beacon return, and that the investigation was complete and would not be pursued further. None of this depends on the Disclosure Project or on any witness, which is exactly why it belongs on this board.

entities.label: Big Sur missile-test filming, September 1964
entities.sub: An Air Force image-orthicon telescope deployment above Big Sur covering Vandenberg launches from August to November 1964, and the subject of two published first-person accounts that agree on who was there and disagree on what was filmed
entities.desc: THE RAREST EVIDENTIARY SHAPE IN THIS CLUSTER: TWO PARTICIPANTS, BOTH PUBLISHED UNDER THEIR OWN NAMES, AGREEING ABOUT THE FACTS OF THE DEPLOYMENT AND DISAGREEING ABOUT ITS PRODUCT. The Air Force placed a borrowed 24-inch Boston University telescope, mounted on a modified five-inch gun mount and fitted with an image orthicon television camera tube, at about 4,000 feet in the Los Padres National Forest above Big Sur, and covered nine of eleven Vandenberg launches between August and November 1964. Lt. Robert Jacobs, named on-site commander by the 1369th Photographic Squadron, published in January 1989 that the resulting film showed a saucer-shaped object circling an Atlas warhead and firing a beam at it. Kingston A. George, the project engineer, published in Winter 1993 that the event was at dawn on 22 September 1964 on a launch nicknamed 'Buzzing Bee', that what was recorded was decoy and chaff deployment giving away the false status of the decoys, that the classified alarm which followed concerned the vulnerability of a weapons system rather than anything extraterrestrial, that Jacobs was not authorised to view the imagery, and that the film was destroyed long before its twelve-year declassification date. George cites a contemporaneous internal document by title and date, which is the best unopened lead this pass produced.

Custody proximity 0: the object at issue is film, not material or craft. Disclosure role 2: the deployment entered public view only through two published participant accounts, twenty-five and twenty-nine years later.

timeline.label: Disclosure Project press conference at the National Press Club
timeline.text: About twenty former government workers spoke, out of sixty-nine whose interviews appear in the accompanying book. ABC News covered it the same day. NO OPENED SOURCE LISTS THE TWENTY; five are placed at the podium by opened sources, namely Callahan, Stone, Filer, Sheehan and Webre.
timeline.source: ABC News, 'Group Calls for Disclosure of UFO Info', 9 May 2001, 2:35 PM, https://abcnews.com/Technology/story?id=98572&page=1

timeline.label: FAA tells a FOIA requester the JAL 1628 records will be destroyed in 30 days
timeline.text: Letter of 27 June 2001: 'all documents pertaining to this UFO sighting will be destroyed in 30 days from the date of this letter.' A further request in 2009 was answered with the statement that the records had been destroyed. Over 1,500 pages were later found at the National Archives.
timeline.source: The Black Vault case file, 'The Vault Files: 1986 Alaska JAL Flight 1628', John Greenewald Jr., https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-vault-files-1986-alaska-jal-flight-1628/

timeline.label: Klass publishes Stone's service record and the 1987 FAA release
timeline.text: Skeptics UFO Newsletter #68, Summer 2001. It prints Clifford Stone's assignment history obtained from the National Personnel Records Center, quotes the FAA Alaskan Region press release of 5 March 1987 and the air traffic control transcript on JAL 1628, and records that twenty of sixty-nine interviewees spoke at the press conference. Klass declares that he was refused admission to the event.
timeline.source: Philip J. Klass, Skeptics UFO Newsletter (SUN) #68, Summer 2001, 'Dr. Greer's Disclosure Conference Reveals His New Strategy'; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/2022/09/26195512/SUN-68-Summer-2001.pdf

timeline.label: A researcher publishes Callahan's self-supplied OMB Form 171
timeline.text: Paul Dean publishes an OMB Form 171 showing 'Division Mgr. Investigations/Evaluations', 'FAA ATS-1 Washington Headquarters', 'Oct. 1986 to present', stating that the originals were provided by Callahan himself in 2015. In part one of the same series Dean had reported his own negative finding: the public record showed a 'Quality Control Branch Manager' of the 'Quality Assurance Staff'.
timeline.source: Paul Dean, 'John Callahan & The JAL-1628 UFO Encounter; FAA Credentials Finally Confirmed, pt2', The UFO Chronicles, https://www.theufochronicles.com/2015/10/john-callahan-jal-1628-ufo-encounter_4.html

timeline.label: Peter Robbins repudiates his co-author after twenty-nine years
timeline.text: Robbins publishes a statement alleging that Larry Warren fabricated a photograph with John Lennon, altered a USAF Form 490 whose ophthalmic notation is attributed to a physician Robbins found to be an orthopaedic surgeon, produced an in-processing sheet with mismatched signatures, and attributed testimonial letters to two named airmen that were never sent. He accepts as authentic Warren's January 1981 letter to his mother.
timeline.source: Peter Robbins, statement regarding Larry Warren, posted 13 June 2017 and updated 20 June 2017, hosted on Sacha Christie's blog, http://sacha-christie-infomaniachousewife.blogspot.com/2017/06/peter-robbins-statement-regarding-larry.html

timeline.label: Publisher suspends distribution of Left at East Gate
timeline.text: Cosimo, Inc.: 'Cosimo is announcing that it is suspending the distribution of the book, Left at East Gate, by Larry Warren and Peter Robbins', because 'some of the experiences described in this book may be inaccurate or embellished'.
timeline.source: Cosimo, Inc., publisher's announcement, 'Announcement: Left at East Gate', http://cosimoblog.blogspot.com/2017/10/announcement-left-at-east-gate.html

timeline.label: Karl Wolfe dies
timeline.text: Karl R. Wolfe, 19 April 1944 to 10 October 2018, per his funeral home obituary at Lansing, New York. The obituary does not mention US Air Force service, an employer, an education or a career, which is the whole of the independent record on him.
timeline.source: Obituary of Karl R. Wolfe, Lansing Funeral Home, Lansing, New York, https://www.lansingfuneralhome.com/obituaries/karl-wolfe

timeline.label: Clifford Stone dies at Roswell
timeline.text: Kevin Randle: 'Clifford E. Stone, known for his relentless pursuit of UFO documentation through his use of FOIA died on February 10, in Roswell, New Mexico.' Randle sets out in the same post the discrepancies between Stone's account and his service record.
timeline.source: Kevin D. Randle, 'Cliff Stone Has Died', A Different Perspective, https://kevinrandle.blogspot.com/2021/02/cliff-stone-has-died.html

gaps.text: THE LARGEST HOLE IN THIS CLUSTER. Twenty of sixty-nine interviewees spoke at the National Press Club on 9 May 2001 and NO OPENED SOURCE LISTS WHICH TWENTY. Five are placed at the podium by opened sources: Callahan, Stone, Filer, Sheehan and Webre. web.archive.org is blocked to this session entirely, so no May 2001 capture of the Project's own site was opened; both WorldCat catalogue records for the event recording returned HTTP 403; no C-SPAN record was found. EVERY PODIUM CLAIM ON THIS BOARD FOR ANY OTHER WITNESS, INCLUDING MARK McCANDLISH, IS UNSUPPORTED UNTIL THIS CLOSES.
gaps.wouldClose: A Wayback capture of disclosureproject.org from May or June 2001; either WorldCat record via a non-403 route; a C-SPAN or other broadcaster's programme record; or a contemporaneous newspaper listing of the speakers.

gaps.text: JOHN CALLAHAN'S CLAIMED TITLE IS UNCORROBORATED BY ANY AGENCY RECORD. The only document is an OMB Form 171 he supplied to a researcher himself in 2015. The researcher's own first pass through the public record found him as 'Quality Control Branch Manager' of the 'Quality Assurance Staff' under the Associate Administrator for Air Traffic, and wrote 'none of them really matched his claimed Accidents, Evaluations and Investigations area'. No FAA release, Federal Register entry, agency directory or personnel record was opened.
gaps.wouldClose: An FAA organisational directory or Federal Register notice for 1985 to 1990 naming the Investigation and Evaluation Division and its manager; a DOT or FAA telephone directory of the period; or an OPM personnel record obtained from the agency rather than from the subject.

gaps.text: NO PAGE OF THE 1,500-PAGE NATIONAL ARCHIVES FILE ON JAL 1628 WAS READ. One PDF was downloaded, 2.8 MB, and is a scan with no text layer; the National Archives catalogue at catalog.archives.gov is a JavaScript application the fetch tool could not render. The file's existence, extent and itemisation are established; its contents are known only through Klass's quotations and The Black Vault's description.
gaps.wouldClose: OCR of the individual PDFs at documents.theblackvault.com; or the NARA catalogue record for archival identifier 733667 retrieved through the NARA API rather than the catalogue front end.

gaps.text: ADMIRAL DONALD ENGEN'S TENURE AS FAA ADMINISTRATOR WAS NOT CONFIRMED FROM ANY FAA SOURCE. faa.gov/about/history/administrators returned HTTP 403. He is named in this cluster only by Callahan and by Klass repeating Callahan, and the briefing Callahan describes rests entirely on that.
gaps.wouldClose: The FAA's own administrators page via a non-403 route; a Federal Register appointment notice; or a Senate confirmation record.

gaps.text: THE BEST UNOPENED LEAD IN THIS CLUSTER. gaps.wouldClose: An Air Force Historical Research Agency holding for 1st Strategic Aerospace Division, 1964; a NARA record group for Air Force Systems Command or the Western Test Range; or a FOIA request to AFHRA naming the study by title and date.
